The French electronic musician Kavinsky, known for the song Nightcall which achieved iconic status after its inclusion in the Ryan Gosling film Drive, has died aged 50. Kavinsky, real name Vincent Belorgey, had reportedly been complaining of headaches in recent days, and he was discovered at home after a concerned neighbour alerted emergency services. Parisian authorities are investigating his death but said “no suspicious elements” were found at his home. Emmanuel Macron was among those paying tribute to him, calling him “a source of French pride forever”.

Kavinsky’s track "Nightcall" sets the cool, atmospheric tone as Ryan Gosling's silent, nameless driver navigates a midnight getaway through Los Angeles. The pairing of Gosling's stoic performance with the electronic track propelled "Nightcall" and the synthwave genre into massive worldwide cult status. Directed by Nicolas Refn, was later released in 2011 and became a significant critical success.
